messages:
rachel: On the call with SummitHealth POC — their Android WebView client is failing to parse SSE streams mid-response. Demo stuck. Need a quick swarm.

aj: What do their client logs show?

rachel: OkHttp logs show: `org.json.JSONException: Unterminated string at character 842` after a chunk boundary. Network shows 200 then socket close ~420ms later. They said the issue only reproduces behind their corporate proxy.

nish: Could be proxy re-buffering or inserting extra CRLFs. Can you grab the raw chunk dump?\r\n

rachel: pasted raw chunked stream from our edge (redacted ids):

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked

5e
data: {"msg":"start","seq":1,"text":"Payload part 1 with unicode ",

3c
data: {"msg":"start","seq":1,"text":"\\u1f600 continued part 2...

0

// socket closed by client, no final newline or event separator
```

rachel: You can see JSON split across chunks and their parser expects each SSE data: line to be a complete JSON object.

aj: Quick mitigations: 1) set `proxy_buffering off` for the streaming vhost so nginx forwards chunks as-is; 2) emit a small minimal `:\n` comment keepalive every 10s to keep proxies from closing; 3) add a lightweight server-side event `event: fragment; data: {"more":true}\n` to signal that JSON continues.

sam: Can you narrow to tenant? This customer is on demo-6789. If it's safe we can flip buffering off just for that tenant. Low blast radius.

nish: Rate limits: I see 429 bursts for demo-6789 earlier — they were retrying aggressively which may trigger intermediate proxies to tear down connections. x-rate-limit-reset was ~20s. I recommend temporarily exempting them while we validate.

deploy-bot: Canary patch queued: config/nginx/demo-6789-streaming-buffering-off @ sha: f1e2d3 (rolling: 1/4 nodes) :gear:

rachel: Customer upgraded their Android wrapper to v1.2.0 which handles split `data:` aggregation. After canary, parse errors dropped to almost zero, but they still reported occasional `Unexpected character '\n' at start of input` when keepalives were comments (just `:\n`).

aj: Some JSON parsers are strict when they don't get a leading `data:` line. Instead of comment-only keepalives, send `data: {}` or `data: "\\n"` to be explicit. Also confirm the corporate proxy isn't collapsing multiple events into a single TCP segment; tcpdump would show that.

nish: I've temporarily relaxed the limiter for demo-6789 for 45m and added an alert suppression rule to avoid noise. Monitoring: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/poc-demo-6789 :mag:

sam: If this recurs after we roll the full patch, plan B is to add a small server-side SSE framing layer that base64-encodes full JSON payloads so intermediate proxies won't split useful bytes. More invasive but reliable.

aj: I'll add `--sse-framing-verbose` logs to the runtime and a small middleware option to emit an `sse-fragment-id` header in each event for correlation. Rolling to canary now.

deploy-bot: Rolling: runtime/sse-framing-verbose @ sha: c4b5a6 (canary 2/4) :rocket:

rachel: Thanks team — AE on the call said the demo recovered once buffering was disabled and the client updated. I'll note the fix in the deal doc and close the ticket after end-to-end verif. :thumbsup:
